sections.content:
Looking at the image, after RIGHT x2:
- Right green box is now to the RIGHT of the right dark gray box (cols ~51-53)
- Left green box is now to the LEFT of its initial position (cols ~15-17), closer to the left dark gray box
So moving the right green box RIGHT causes the left green box to move LEFT! This is the inverse relationship I suspected.
The left green box moved from cols 18-20 to cols 15-17 (3 columns LEFT) when the right green box moved from cols 45-47 to cols 51-53 (6 columns RIGHT). So the ratio is 6:3 = 2:1. For every 2 columns the right green box moves RIGHT, the left green box moves 1 column LEFT.
The left green box needs to move from cols 15-17 to cols 12-14 to be inside the left dark gray box. That's 3 columns LEFT. So the right green box needs to move 6 columns RIGHT, which is RIGHT x2 (since each RIGHT moves the right green box 3 columns).
But wait, the right green box is already at cols 51-53, which is to the RIGHT of the right dark gray box. If I move RIGHT x2 more, the right green box will be at cols 57-59, and the left green box will be at cols 12-14, inside the left dark gray box.
Let me try RIGHT x2 to see if the left green box moves inside the left dark gray box.
But also, the left green box is at rows 30-32, and the left dark gray box interior is at rows 33-35. So the left green box needs to move DOWN by 3 rows as well. Does moving the right green box RIGHT also move the left green box DOWN?
Let me check the current segmentation to see the exact positions.

- Currently left green at cols 15-17, rows 30-32
